learning_outcomes.text: The graduate has the necessary knowledge for using computers, developing software programs and applications, information processing.
The graduate is able to identify complex problems and examine related issues to develop solving options and implement solutions.
The graduate is able to combine diverse information to formulate solutions and generate ideas for developing new products and applications.
The graduate has the ability to apply general rules to specific problems and produce relevant solutions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Data structures. Abstract Data Types.
Abstract Data Types and Data Structures
ADT Set: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT Map: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT Matrix: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT MultiMap: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT Stack: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT Queue: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT PriorityQueue: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT Deque: description, domain, interface and possible representations
ADT List : description, domain, interface and possible representations
Singly linked list: representation and operations
Doubly linked list: representation and operations
Sorted linked lists: representation and operations
Circular linked lists: representation and operations
Linked lists on arrays: representation and operations
Description and properties of binary trees
Domain and interface of ADT Binary Tree
Possible representations of ADT Binary Tree
Containers represented over binary search trees
Applications and data structure libraries in different programming languages
Lab1. A1- Dynamic array - Example of a solved lab assignment (Demo)
Lab 2. Discussion about the Demo. Example of an extra operation
Lab 3. A2 - Linked lists with dynamic allocation
Lab 4. A3 - Linked lists on array
Lab 7. Presentation of problem from Lab 6
ADT Bag with generic elements. Representations and implementation on an array. Iterator for ADT Bag
Bucket sort, Lexicographic sort, radix sort. Merging two sorted singly linked lists.
Sorted MultiMap – representation and implementation on a singly linked list
Evaluating an arithmetic expression. Problems solved with binary heap.

assessment_methods.method: Written evaluation (written exam in the exam session)
Lab assignment (C++ implementation, correctness, documentation, respecting deadlines)
Seminar activity (active participation, asking/answering questions, volunteering to solve problems)

assessment_rules: For participating in the written exam, a student must have at least 6 lab attendances and 5 seminar attendances. To pass, a student must score at least 5 on the written exam and have a minimum final grade of 5. Active participation in the seminar can earn a maximum of 0.5 bonus points, added to the final grade.
